episodes.170458: A thunderstorm became severe in Orange County, where it produced hail and wind damage near Bay Lake and Windermere.
episodes.170633: Isolated thunderstorms produced gusty outflow winds across a station or two in central and eastern Nevada.
episodes.170666: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.170731: An upper level ridge was centered to the east of the Four Corners region. An upper level disturbance moved over West Texas and provided a source of lift. The air near the surface was relatively dry compared to the air in the middle levels of the atmosphere. These conditions resulted in a thunderstorm that produced a severe wind gust in the Permian Basin.
episodes.170754: An isolated severe thunderstorm affected a small portion of Prince William County during the evening hours.
episodes.170755: A couple of isolated severe thunderstorms produced localized wind damage from east-central Virginia into southern Maryland.
episodes.170756: A couple of isolated severe thunderstorms produced localized wind damage from east-central Virginia into southern Maryland.
episodes.170841: A thunderstorm produced localized gusty winds over the tidal Potomac River.
episodes.170948: A shortwave trough brought scattered thunderstorms to Central New York. The environment was unstable enough for a couple of thunderstorms to become severe. One thunderstorm produced a microburst with estimated winds of 90 mph. Most of the damage was trees and corn stalks knocked down, though there was also some structual damage to farm buildings.
episodes.171104: Several clusters of thunderstorms moved through northeast Louisiana on the afternoon and evening of July 13th. A number of these storms were severe and produced damaging wind gusts that downed trees and power lines. Large hail up to quarter size was also observed.
episodes.171317: Thunderstorms developed across Downeast areas during the afternoon of the 14th. An isolated severe thunderstorm produced damaging downburst winds in a wooded area near Grand Lake Stream in Washington county.
episodes.171369: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a trough of low pressure in a very hot airmass. Some of these storms produced strong, damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171575: The synoptic pattern was characterized by an area of high pressure centered across the four corners region with a southeasterly steering flow encompassing all of Arizona. MLCAPE between 500-1000 J/KG and DCAPE in excess of 1500 J/KG were more than sufficient to lead to the development of thunderstorm activity, first developing across southeast Arizona and then being steered by the southeasterly flow into south-central Arizona. Portions of the East Valley got particularly hit hard between Gilbert and Mesa, where there were several reports of wind damage. No injuries were reported.
episodes.171745: A cluster of thunderstorms developed along the southeast Georgia coast and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.171746: Thunderstorms first developed along the sea breeze in the early afternoon hours on the southeast South Carolina coast. The thunderstorms then shifted inland along an outflow boundary and became nearly stationary across the Charleston Tri-County region. The thunderstorms repeatedly passed through an area from around Summerville and North Charleston. Extremely heavy rainfall occurred, producing flash flooding in this region. Thunderstorms also impacted the Walterboro area, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171747: Thunderstorms first developed along the sea breeze on the southeast Georgia coast. One thunderstorm became strong enough to produce hail in Chatham County.
episodes.171817: Showers and thunderstorms formed along a sea breeze boundary across Long Island. One of the thunderstorms was able to become severe and caused damaging winds as well as large hail in Central Long Island.
episodes.171899: A cold front was stalling in northern Mississippi on the morning of the 13th. Storms began to develop ahead of the boundary across central Mississippi around midday and were moving southward towards the local area. As they approached southwest Mississippi, the storms intensified as a result of entering a region of ample instability. The resultant squall-line produced damaging winds across Pike County.
episodes.171965: Several rounds of severe weather occurred during the July 9-13 time frame. These rounds of thunderstorms were the result of two cold fronts moving across the state in association with a surface low moving along the boundary.
episodes.171978: A supercell thunderstorm resulted in multiple severe wind damage reports over Ulster and Dutchess Counties during the evening of Wednesday July 13, 2022. Additionally, the supercell resulted in a tornado and macroburst in Ulster County near Kingston, NY. The Mayor announced a Local State of Emergency (restricting all un-necessary travel in and around Kingston) after thunderstorms produced extensive tree damage in the area. At one point, over 6,000 residents were without power in the city of Kingston.
episodes.171985: On July 13th, thunderstorms developed in northwestern Kansas during the evening hours associated with a surface trough in the region. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts up to an estimated 90 mph and hail up to quarters in size.
episodes.172201: A strong thunderstorm moved across northern Park and Big Horn Counties and brought high wind gusts. Wind gusts of 70 and 64 mph were reported at the Greybull and Powell airports, respectively. No damage was reported.
episodes.172212: Isolated thunderstorms developed across the Pikes Peak region on this day, and then moved into the I-25 corridor in the evening. While most storms were sub severe, an isolated wind gust to 58 mph was observed near the Air Force Academy.
episodes.172245: Thunderstorms developed along and south of a stationary front the afternoon of July 14 as an upper level disturbance dropped southwest through the region. Damaging wind gusts and hail occurred with a few of these storms near and just south of the DFW Metroplex.
episodes.172363: Moist southwesterly flow prevailed as the Atlantic ridge extended into northeast Florida. Showers and storms moved northeastward across the area and interacted with the pinned Atlantic sea breeze boundary along I-95 in Flagler county. A lightning strike from a passing thunderstorm struck a house in Flagler County Wednesday evening.
episodes.172365: Showers and thunderstorms developed along a cold front which pushed through Kentucky during the afternoon and evening hours on July 12th. Immediately ahead of the front, temperatures in the upper 80s and lower 90s combined with dewpoints in the mid-70s to facilitate the development of greater than 3000 J/kg mixed-layer CAPE. With plenty of fuel to work with, storms grew rapidly, especially across south central Kentucky, leading to isolated wind damage reports in association with the strongest cells.||On July 14th, the mid-level trough which brought the cold front and associated thunderstorms through Kentucky two days prior began to shift off to the east. A weak surface frontal boundary developed over portions of southwestern Kentucky, and frontal convergence along with modest instability helped contribute to the development of scattered strong thunderstorms across southern and central Kentucky. One of these storms was just strong enough to produce scattered wind damage across Grayson County.
episodes.172372: Isolated afternoon thunderstorms developed across much of west central Texas. A few storms were severe and produced wind damage. On July 12th, a significant microburst was reported in Tom Green County, 6 miles east of Arden.
episodes.172383: A strong high pressure system centered near the Four Corners and a decaying  thunderstorm complex over northwest Mexico brought additional moisture across western Arizona.  This brought strong thunderstorm activity will be along and southwest of|a line from extending from the Grand Canyon southeastward through Flagstaff and Happy Jack.
episodes.172505: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots as well as a few sightings of waterspouts.
episodes.172536: A strong and persistent upper-level ridge across the Four Corners Region retrograded slightly westward, allowing an upper-level trough to shift southward from the Plains and Ozarks. The trough helped to drive a weak frontal boundary in the region where ample instability was in place as daytime maximum temperatures averaged between 100-105 degrees on July 13th. Convection began to form by mid to late afternoon with several thunderstorms quickly becoming severe in the very unstable conditions. The high-based thunderstorms presented a primary damaging wind threat, which resulted in numerous damage reports through the afternoon and evening hours on the 13th. Some of the severe thunderstorms also produced hail of various sizes, including a few reports of large hail.
episodes.172537: A strong and persistent upper-level ridge across the Four Corners Region retrograded slightly westward, allowing an upper-level trough to shift southward from the Plains and Ozarks. The trough helped to drive a weak frontal boundary in the region where ample instability was in place as daytime maximum temperatures averaged between 100-105 degrees on July 13th. Convection began to form by mid to late afternoon with several thunderstorms quickly becoming severe in the very unstable conditions. The high-based thunderstorms presented a primary damaging wind threat, which resulted in numerous damage reports through the afternoon and evening hours on the 13th. Some of the severe thunderstorms also produced hail of various sizes, including a few reports of large hail. These storms continued through the early morning hours of the 14th before diminishing. Additional isolated severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 14th over Eastern Smith County, producing damaging winds that tore a portion of the roof off of the Chapel Hill High School cafeteria.
episodes.172599: A mid-level disturbance and surface trough draped from western North Carolina into south-central Virginia led to development of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across the northwest Piedmont in the late afternoon. These storms tracked east-southeast during the mid to late-evening hours, tapering off by late evening. The storms over Orange and Durham Counties produced flash flooding around Chapel Hill and Durham.
episodes.172600: Thunderstorms brought severe weather to southeast Idaho.
episodes.172617: A second consecutive day of thunderstorms brought reports of significant outflow gusts.
episodes.172621: An active summer setup resulted in multiple reports of weather incidents, including microburst related wind gusts in portions of Utah's West Desert, a landspout, and flash flooding which included burn scar debris flows.
episodes.172667: Thunderstorms produced damaging winds and locally heavy rainfall over Victoria. The winds blew down a tree over the road in Mission Valley and heavy rain caused flooding of streets on the northwest side of Victoria.
episodes.172722: An upper level low pressure system and strong divergent flow aloft combined with a muggy airmass to create an unstable airmass on the afternoon of July 14th across Maine.  Morning cloud cover limited daytime heating, but enough clearing allowed for a line of thunderstorms to develop across the I-95 corridor.  A few strong storms developed along with and isolated severe thunderstorm.
episodes.172804: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours across portions of eastern North Dakota and west-central Minnesota.
episodes.172805: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours across portions of eastern North Dakota and west-central Minnesota.
episodes.172886: A push of monsoon moisture fueled an outbreak of thunderstorms across the Mojave Desert. Some storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.172887: A push of monsoon moisture fueled an outbreak of thunderstorms across the Mojave Desert. Some storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.172951: High moisture and seabreezes led to the formation of afternoon thunderstorms along the Gulf coast of SW Florida.
episodes.172970: Waterspouts developed in association with showers and thunderstorms developing as eastward-propagating outflow boundaries moved against ambient east-southeast flow.
